elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 retains "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other," and the notice "shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" — an unconditional Company election, i.e., a convenience right over the Agreement (no Order Form structure exists here). Section 4.1(a) presupposes the same right ("In the event the Company terminates this Agreement").

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The Company's notice period remains ninety (90) days; no operation reduces it to 30 days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in the rendered text; the only money mechanic runs the other way (Company pays HDI the Termination Payment).

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Insert: "Any termination by HDI under this Section 4.1 shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term..." — HDI cannot exit during the one-year committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 4.1: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other," with the terminating Party's notice fixing the Termination Date; 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band and the term-end limitation was inserted only against HDI, so the Company's right is unrestricted as to timing. The deterministic 'Customer convenience termination present' flag is false, but on substance the mutual unconditional election plus clause (a)'s premise of Company termination establishes the right.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Insert: "In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the fees payable to HDI under Section 3 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." This caps the Net-Sales-minus-$800,000 formula at three months of fees; the instalment mechanic in (c) merely schedules payment of the (now capped) amount.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Insert expressly ties the effective date to term end: "effective only at the end of the then-current term, and any Termination Date specified in HDI's notice shall be the last day of that term" — satisfying the rule that an auto-renewal notice right is not term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly so tied.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 4.1 requires "ninety (90) days written notice" from either Party; the insert restricts the effective date but does not shorten notice.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the Company keeps a 90-day convenience exit, HDI's 4.1 termination is now effective only at term end, HDI's 90-day notice is retained, and the Termination Payment is capped at three months of Section 3 fees. Deviation status and the fallback target are correctly chosen.

Preferred fails on two elements the drafter correctly declined to pursue: 30-day Company notice and a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Rationale properly notes these as accepted shortfalls rather than redlining them.

Minimality holds: two short inserts, no deletions, no survival tails, expense language, or extra procedures; the retained favourable formula (Net Sales less $800,000, divided by two) survives subject only to the cap. The trailing words of insert 1 ('any Termination Date specified in HDI's notice shall be the last day of that term') are necessary, not surplus, because the retained sentence otherwise lets HDI's notice pick any date and would contradict the term-end limit.

Intent preserved: HDI's for-cause or other termination rights outside Section 4.1 are untouched (the insert is expressly scoped to 'under this Section 4.1'), the quarterly instalment mechanic in (c) still operates on the capped amount, and the defined term 'Termination Date' remains coherent.

Verify before sending: the cap references 'fees payable to HDI under Section 3.' Confirm Section 3 is in fact the compensation/fees section and that Company consideration to HDI is styled as 'fees' rather than a revenue share on Net Sales; if the latter, replace with 'amounts payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3' to avoid an undefined or nil-value cap and a dangling cross-reference.

Optional hardening (not a defect at fallback): Section 4.1's termination right sits inside the auto-renewal sentence, which invites an argument that it is only a non-renewal mechanic. A three-word clarifier — 'terminated by either Party at any time upon ninety (90) days written notice' — would put the Company's convenience right beyond doubt without disturbing the HDI-side term-end limit.
